text:
Aditya Rao: We need to lock beta cohort selection for Suggestions view by EOW. Can we align on enable criteria + how we collect feedback without turning this into a week-by-week scope negotiation with eng?

Marissa Cole: +1. From Console side: we can only support a small set initially (read-only behind `suggestions_beta` + allowlist). If we pick folks with messy RBAC setups or low telemetry coverage we’ll spend all our time on “why is it empty” instead of UX signal.

Chris Osei: Can we define cohort in 2 buckets?
1) “good telemetry / high chance of seeing suggestions” (primary)
2) “edge cases” (secondary, for validation but not the first wave)
So enable wave 1 doesn’t get derailed.

Jasmine Liu: CS perspective: wave 1 should be customers who are already asking “how do I lower $/1M tokens” and have someone who will actually join the feedback loop. If we enable 15 tenants and no one looks at it, we’ll get false negatives.

Rachel Kim: Agree. For enterprise, I’d add: they need a named admin + a security-aware stakeholder we can route questions to. Otherwise we’ll get stuck on “who can see cost data” debates mid-beta.

Miguel Santos: Proposed wave 1 criteria (enterprise cohort):
- Dedicated or high-volume Hosted (so savings estimates aren’t tiny)
- Stable traffic week-to-week (avoid huge variance first)
- Willing to do 30-min onboarding + 15-min weekly check-in
- Has at least one route pinned to a known model version (less confounding)
- No “must be on-prem” or air-gapped requirements for the beta

Aparna Reddy: For mid-market/self-serve: similar but we can relax the “weekly check-in” to async feedback if they’re responsive. Biggest thing: they need to have enough recent usage for baselines.

Logan Wright: Telemetry gate suggestion:
- baseline freshness < 24h (if older, UI will show “insufficient data”)
- token metering present for route+model+region for last 7d window
- no known ingestion lag incidents for that tenant
We can run a query and give CS a “green/yellow/red” list.

Marissa Cole: +1 to making telemetry health an explicit gate. Otherwise the Suggestions view looks broken and we’ll get UX feedback that’s really data quality.

Dev Patel: Support ask: please don’t enable any tenant unless we have:
- the canned FAQ ready (what “risk” means, why savings changes)
- a clear escalation path (support -> CS -> product/eng)
We already have tickets where “estimates changed week over week” becomes a multi-day thread.

Aditya Rao: Makes sense. Can we agree on numbers? I was thinking ~10 tenants in wave 1, then +10 in wave 2 after a week of telemetry + UI sanity.

Chris Osei: 10 in wave 1 is reasonable. We should define “exit criteria” for wave 1 so we don’t keep it small forever:
- <2% Suggestions page load errors
- <5% “insufficient telemetry” among enabled tenants (or we understand why)
- qualitative: at least 5 users can correctly explain “savings estimate basis” after walkthrough

George Mbatha: For capturing feedback without blocking engineering: recommend we separate feedback streams:
1) Usability issues (IA/copy/confusion) -> Design/PM bucket
2) Data quality/coverage issues -> Telemetry/ML bucket
3) Feature requests (“apply button”, exports) -> Phase 2 backlog
And we time-box wave 1 research to a fixed set of sessions. Otherwise every loud request becomes a stop-the-line.

Marissa Cole: Yes please. Also: we should be strict that beta is read-only. We can’t accept “we won’t use it unless it applies automatically” as a blocker for shipping the beta.

Aditya Rao: +1. Let’s write enable criteria as a checklist and treat anything outside as “wave 2 / later.”

Rachel Kim: One nuance: some enterprise customers will want this enabled but only for a subset of admins. Can we require they confirm who will have access + that they’re okay with viewing cost-derived suggestions?

Marissa Cole: Console has RBAC + audit logging in progress, but for beta we can require “Org Admin / Billing Admin” only. We can document that. If they need custom roles, that’s wave 2.

Logan Wright: If we do that, please make sure the allowlist workflow captures:
- tenant/workspace id
- which roles are expected to see it
So we can debug “I can’t see Suggestions” quickly.

Dev Patel: Also: can we create one public-ish place for feedback? Not 15 DMs. Suggest:
- a shared Google form for structured feedback (screenshot upload + route/model)
- plus a single email alias for “beta-suggestions@…” that routes to Support+CS

Chris Osei: I can set up the form + a lightweight triage doc. But we need agreement: product triages weekly, engineering only sees summarized P0/P1 issues, not raw feedback spam.

Aditya Rao: Exactly. Let’s set a rule:
- P0 = tenant isolation / security / major correctness bug
- P1 = broken UI states (empty due to bug) + clearly wrong estimates
- P2 = copy tweaks, nicer filters, etc.
Only P0/P1 create interrupts during wave 1.

Marissa Cole: Works. Also link feedback to artifacts we already have:
- Linear for actionable bugs
- a single “beta feedback themes” doc updated weekly
Eng shouldn’t have to attend every check-in.

Jasmine Liu: From CS: we can own the weekly customer check-ins and send a 1-pager summary (top 3 pain points + top 3 wins) to this channel. If something is a P0/P1, we’ll tag product + the right eng owner.

Miguel Santos: I’ll draft the initial cohort list with owners + readiness notes. We should explicitly avoid:
- tenants with highly spiky workloads (we already know risk scoring gets weird)
- anyone currently mid-migration (new routes/models weekly)

Aparna Reddy: +1. For mid-market, I have 3 candidates who are already asking about caching/batching and have consistent traffic. I’ll send names to Chris (not in-thread).

George Mbatha: Can we bake in one “friendly skeptic” customer in wave 1? Someone likely to challenge trust/explainability. Better to learn early, but only one so we don’t get derailed.

Aditya Rao: Good call. One skeptic, not five.

Marissa Cole: Action items:
- Chris: enable criteria checklist + feedback intake form + triage process (share link here)
- Logan: telemetry health query + green/yellow/red output for cohort candidates
- CS (Jasmine/Rachel/Miguel/Aparna): propose wave 1 list (10) w/ commitment to feedback cadence
I’ll make sure Console can handle allowlist + role gating in prod without drama.

Chris Osei: On it. I’ll also add “do not block eng” language explicitly: beta feedback is input, not a re-scope.

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: once the FAQ draft is ready, please loop Support for wording. We want consistent answers for “why did savings change” and “what does high risk mean.”

Aditya Rao: Great. Let’s aim to confirm wave 1 by Friday noon PT so Dylan/Chloe can plan flag flips early next week.

(Linear bot): Chris Osei created task PM-413 “Beta enablement plan + support readiness (FAQ, escalation path, weekly feedback cadence, exit criteria)” and linked this thread.

Marissa Cole: :+1: thanks. Also, please keep cohort comms consistent: “beta is read-only, estimates are directional, risk is guidance.” No promises on guaranteed savings.

Jasmine Liu: Copy that. We’ll set expectations in the onboarding email + walkthrough.

Aditya Rao: Closing the loop: if anyone disagrees with the gates (telemetry freshness, role constraints, cadence), say it today so we don’t churn tomorrow.
